verdict.reasoning: Patient states diarrhea for "past three days" and frequency "around five to six times a day" with "definitely watery" loose stools.
Patient reports "diarrhea for like, let's say, past three days" and going "around five to six times a day" with "definitely watery" loose stools.
Patient says it "started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times, but then that went away" and later confirms "The vomiting is now stopped."
In response to blood in stool, patient says: "No, not that I could see."
When asked about tummy pain, patient replies: "Not. Not really, no."

Patient says "I feel very dehydrated" and describes not drinking enough, plus "Not much. Not much. So just a little bit, but I don't really feel like I have appetite," indicating decreased intake and appetite.
Patient reports early fever: "Probably at the beginning I was feeling. I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel kind of fine" and adds "I feel very weak, though."
When asked about headaches, patient answers: "Not really."
When asked about muscle pains, patient again answers: "Not really," indicating no myalgias.
Regarding triggers, patient says: "Not that I. That I remember" and just describes being at home working when symptoms started.
When asked about takeaway or "dodgy restaurant food," patient replies: "Not that I remember," indicating no suspect food exposure.
Doctor asks about being around anyone unwell with diarrhea; patient replies: "Not that I know," indicating no sick contacts.
Patient states: "So I do suffer of asthma."
Patient notes using inhalers "infrequently" and confirms it is a blue inhaler, consistent with as-needed use.
To question about allergies, patient replies: "Not that I know of."
Patient says: "My father has high. Well, used to have high blood pressure."
Patient reports: "He actually died of bowel cancer like 10 years ago."
Patient says of mother: "she has diabetes" and clarifies "It's type two."
When asked who lives at home, patient answers: "Oh, I live alone."
When asked employment, patient states: "I'm a software engineer."
Patient says: "These last three days I've been feeling really unwell, so I couldn't work," indicating 3 days off work.
On smoking, patient says: "and I don't smoke."
On alcohol, patient says: "I drink infrequently, like socially, let's say."
Doctor states: "I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis" and symptoms are watery diarrhea for "about three days" as previously detailed.
Patient confirms: "Yes" when doctor asks, "The vomiting is now stopped. Is that right?"
Patient denies blood: "No, not that I could see" when asked about blood in stools.
Patient describes feeling "very dehydrated" and unable to keep up with fluids, consistent with dehydration symptoms.
Patient reports prior fever/temperature and current weakness; doctor later mentions paracetamol "if you're feeling feverish and weak," indicating mild systemic symptoms.
Doctor advises: "drink plenty of fluids" and "You can get things from the pharmacy, which called Diurelite... a type of fluid replacement drink."
Doctor states: "You can take some paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak."
Doctor advises: "continue taking time off work for next day or two" and "Normally you have to be diarrhea free for about 24 to 48 hours before you return back to work."
Doctor says: "if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me and we can have another look at your symptoms."
